change.title: ao-replay/8832-r1
change.description: perf(chat): open and switch chats without waiting on workspace reads
change.author: Dhruv Sharma

findings.title: Paths endpoint lists files deleted in the worktree; the old client-side filter is gone
findings.body:
The old client (`useWorkspaceFilePaths`, `NewChatPage`) dropped `status === "deleted"` rows, with a comment that offering a deleted path inserts a reference the agent cannot resolve. The new endpoint does not drop them, so the filter is lost on every path that returns this endpoint's data.

`workspaceSourcePaths` takes its inventory from `git ls-files -co` (`workspace_files.go:1806`). `-c` lists every index entry whether or not the file still exists on disk. A tracked file removed with plain `rm` (the usual way an agent deletes one), or a staged-then-removed file, therefore stays in `paths`. The `@` menu will offer it.

When `total > limit` the code also merges `changes.changedPaths()` (`workspace_files.go:1857`). That set contains every status key, including committed and uncommitted deletions, so deleted files are added there too. The 'keep changed files when capped' test only covers a modified file.

`TestListWorkspaceFilePathsMatchesFullListWithoutDeletions` misses this. It deletes with `git rm`, which also removes the index entry, so the file is absent from `ls-files`. Its `listedPaths` helper filters deleted rows, so an unstaged `rm` would make `got` and `want` differ and fail the test.

Fix: drop paths whose `changes.statuses[rel] == WorkspaceFileDeleted` before returning. `resolveWorkspaceChanges` is cached and shared with the file-list endpoint. Alternatively subtract `git ls-files -z -d` from the inventory. Add a test that deletes a tracked file with `os.Remove` and asserts it is absent, both under and over the limit.

`SearchWorkspaceFiles` has the same list as input. Before this PR it also returned deleted rows, since it never filtered them, so leave its behavior alone unless you decide otherwise.

findings.title: JSDoc for useWorkspaceFilePaths now sits on fetchWorkspaceFilePaths
findings.body: `fetchWorkspaceFilePaths` was inserted between the `/** Every path in the session worktree... */` block (2216-2224) and `useWorkspaceFilePaths` (2240). The doc now describes the fetch helper and the hook has none. Its text is also stale: it says the daemon 'already serves this list' and 'caps itself', but the helper now calls a dedicated endpoint and falls back to the file list. Move the block back above the hook and give the helper its own short comment about the `ROUTE_NOT_FOUND` fallback.

findings.title: Why is the workspaces refresh on chat-view activation dropped?
findings.body: The block now only invalidates the conversation query. The `workspaceQueryKeyForHost(hostId)` invalidation is gone, and the test that asserted it was inverted (`SessionView.test.tsx:1873`). The new comment says clearing the sleep marker on wake emits no event, which is the situation where the workspace list would also stay stale. Does any workspace-list field the UI reads (status/activity shown in the header or sidebar) change on that wake and now go stale until the next event or poll? I could not find a consumer that breaks. `needsResume` comes from `rec.NeedsImportResume()` (`service.go:1943`) and is handled by the resume mutation's `onSettled`. Please say which field this was costing time on and why it is safe to skip.

contracts.action: New GET /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/workspace/paths endpoint returning visible file paths only
contracts.equivalent_path: GET /workspace/files (listWorkspaceFiles) via Service.ListWorkspaceFiles, whose rows the client then filtered to non-deleted paths
contracts.before_after: Old: full file summaries with per-file status/size, then client dropped deleted rows. New: service builds path-only inventory from git ls-files, merging changed paths only when over the cap. It never filters deleted files, which the old client did.
contracts.visible_effect: The @-mention menu and new-chat file list read from this endpoint. Deleted-but-still-indexed files would appear in the menu.
contracts.failure_mode: Service errors go through envelope.WriteError. A nil Svc returns 501. A nil Paths slice is normalised to [] so JSON has an empty array. The frontend falls back to /workspace/files only on ROUTE_NOT_FOUND.

contracts.action: SearchWorkspaceFiles now searches the path inventory and builds summaries only for the returned page
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously ListWorkspaceFiles (full summaries, capped at maxWorkspaceFiles=5000) then substring filter
contracts.before_after: Before: capped at 5000 files, with truncated reflecting the file-browser cap. After: cap is maxWorkspaceFilePaths=20000, and per-result summaries come from resolveWorkspaceChanges (cached/singleflight) plus workspaceFileSizeAndBinary. Fingerprint uses the same summaryFingerprint as finalizeWorkspaceFiles, and Editable is not part of the result. Scratch workspaces use the old scratch listing.
contracts.visible_effect: File search finds files past 5000 and returns the same status/size/binary/fingerprint as the file list. Tests compare them.
contracts.failure_mode: A summary error for any returned path fails the whole search with that error, not a partial result.

contracts.action: Frontend fetchWorkspaceFilePaths with ROUTE_NOT_FOUND fallback to /workspace/files
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous inline GET /workspace/files in useWorkspaceFilePaths and NewChatPage
contracts.before_after: Before: one request, client-side deleted filter. After: tries /paths; on a ROUTE_NOT_FOUND error code (the router 404 in httpd/api.go:465) retries /workspace/files and filters deleted rows client-side. useWorkspaceFilePaths now passes the query's AbortSignal. NewChatPage does not.
contracts.visible_effect: Remote hosts running an older daemon still get a menu. A path-endpoint session-not-found 404 has a different code and is returned as-is.
contracts.failure_mode: A reject on the fallback request propagates to the query. useWorkspaceFilePaths records it via recordWorkspaceResult, and NewChatPage throws it into react-query.

contracts.action: File-path query in SessionChatSurface is enabled only after the composer reports an @ query
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously enabled whenever snapshot existed and the session did not need resume
contracts.before_after: fileMenuAsked is local state, set by onFileQuery, which ChatComposer calls whenever fileQuery !== undefined. SessionChatSurface is rendered with key={uiSessionId}, so the flag does not leak across sessions on remount or switch.
contracts.visible_effect: No workspace read on chat open. The first @ in the composer triggers the fetch, so the first menu shows an empty list until it loads.
contracts.failure_mode: If the paths request fails, the error is recorded and the query does not retry (retry:false). The menu stays empty with no visible error, which matches the prior behavior.

contracts.action: Route loader prefetches the conversation for an opened local chat session
contracts.before_after: Sidebar skips when the query data already exists, the base URL is untrusted, or the session is not a local chat. It also skips cloud sessions and, for the remote variant, uses the host key. The loader repeats these guards and also skips needsResume. It reads the session from the cached workspaces list, so it does nothing when that list is not loaded yet. It uses the local key only, which is right since this route has no hostId.
contracts.visible_effect: The chat page can paint from a conversation fetch that started with route load.
contracts.failure_mode: prefetchInfiniteQuery swallows errors and is not awaited, so a failure leaves the normal useConversation fetch to retry.

summary: The new /workspace/paths endpoint, the OpenAPI/schema.ts additions, the search rewrite and the frontend fallback are consistent with each other. One real regression: the endpoint no longer drops files deleted in the worktree, which the old client filtered. A plain `rm` of a tracked file leaves it in `git ls-files -co`, and it also appears among the changed paths once the list passes the cap. The only deletion test uses `git rm`, so it misses this. Two lesser items: the useWorkspaceFilePaths doc comment is now attached to the new helper, and the removed workspaces invalidation in SessionView needs a rationale.
